162	The question is asked, which the Radak asks: what does it mean to say about
163	HaShem that He does not take a bribe? Where
164	does the bribe come into this matter of not taking a bribe?
165	The Ramban comes in the weekly parashah and, in a few words, speaks
166	at length, in a few words, he speaks briefly on this subject
167	of not taking a bribe. The Ramban writes: even a perfect chasid
168	who commits a transgression, may it not befall us, a single chasid,
169	chasid meaning a person of great virtue. It does not mean
170	a chasid that you associate with the notion of Chassidim or
171	Litaim. So I will speak with you about a chasid. This is
172	a person of great stature. We all know that chasidut
173	is on the scale of values of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, a very
174	high level. Even a perfect chasid who commits
175	a transgression, He will not take one of his mitzvot as a bribe
176	to atone for him. There is no such situation, writes the Ramban, that HaShem
177	removes one mitzvah and atones for him
178	for the transgression. No, rather He will punish him for his sins
179	and will repay him in full for all his good deeds. HaShem does not
180	take mitzvot as a bribe and say, you committed a transgression,
181	please, come, I will deduct it. Rather, what? Very simply, he says:
182	you will receive punishment for the transgression and you will receive reward for
183	the mitzvah. These are the words of the Ramban. What is said here, "does not
184	take a bribe": the same words can also be found
185	in Rabbeinu Ovadia Sforno, who writes: "He will not remove at all
186	from the punishment of the transgression for the sake of the merit of a mitzvah that he did."
187	There is no such thing as His removing any of the punishment for the transgression
188	for the sake of the merit of one mitzvah, because, as they said, as it is written
189	in the Gemara, in tractate Sotah, page 21, one mitzvah does not extinguish
190	a transgression. A mitzvah does not manage to extinguish a transgression. And all this
191	teaches that you should not trust, if you sin, to be saved by any merit
192	from the punishment at all. There is no situation in which you would say, listen,
193	I committed a transgression, let them deduct mitzvot for me. There is no such thing.
194	No mitzvot will be deducted for you, except through complete
195	teshuvah. Only if a person repents can the transgression
196	be removed. There is no way to remove
197	a transgression in exchange for a mitzvah. These are the words of Rabbeinu Ovadia
198	Sforno, which come from the Ramban, with a bit more elaboration
199	of these matters. These are explained more fully, at much

203	in Pirkei Avot: five chapters of mishnayot and one baraita
204	of Kinyan Torah. And there, in the last Mishnah of chapter 5,
205	Mishnah 22: "He used to say: those who are born are to die, and the dead
206	are to live, and the living are to be judged, to make known and to teach that He
207	is," says the Mishnah, "the Maker, He is the Creator, He is the
208	Discerner. This is up to here the introduction. Now we come
209	to the system of judgment. He is the Judge, He is the Witness, He is
210	the Litigant, and He is going to judge, blessed is He. These are
211	the words, these are the words that appear. He is going to
212	judge, blessed is He, says the Mishnah, before whom there is
213	neither forgetfulness, nor lapse of memory, nor favoritism, nor taking
214	of bribes. He has neither this, nor that, nor that. So
215	says the Mishnah: before Him there is no forgetfulness, no lapse of memory,
216	no favoritism, and no taking of bribes, for everything is His. Rabbi
217	Yaavetz says in his commentary on this Mishnah: we have
218	here four things that relate to the system of judgment:
219	judge, witness, litigant, and "He is going to judge." Against
220	these there are: no forgetfulness, no lapse of memory, no favoritism, and no
221	taking of bribes. What corresponds to what? He says: "He is the Judge"
222	corresponds to "before Him there is no forgetfulness," and therefore there is no judge better
223	than Him. Yaavetz writes: He is the best Judge.
224	"He is the Witness" corresponds to "no lapse of memory," for one who forgets his testimony cannot
225	testify; one who does not remember details cannot
226	testify. How is HaShem the Witness? He does not
227	forget, there is no lapse of memory. "He is the Litigant" and He collects from
228	His creatures, He collects from His creatures for the sins
229	they committed, and this corresponds to "no favoritism."
230	"And He is going to judge" corresponds to "no taking of bribes," and He does not
231	need to disqualify Himself out of concern for bias, as we find
232	that certain judges disqualified themselves: one dusted off
233	his coat, and another brought him all kinds of things,
234	and they were disqualified from judging. He says: with HaShem
235	there is no such thing. He is going to judge, because there is no
236	question that He takes a bribe, and therefore He can judge;
237	He does not need to recuse Himself. That is all that appears
238	there in the Mishnah. With the help of Heaven. "And know that everything is according to the reckoning,"
239	says the Mishnah, "and let your inclination not assure you that the grave is a place of refuge…"
